signal_or_function: K_DISCH / active discharge vs a closed main contactor
finding: Any E-stop or chain trip de-energises K_DISCH (DO5 is behind 24V_DO switches A and B and gated by GATE_EN), which puts the 1.5 kOhm / 100 W discharge resistor across the port bus. The port's hold-closed interlock deliberately keeps the main contactor closed after an E-stop for up to 197 s (fault current 382-442 A until the fuse clears), and a welded contact (D-019 residual risk) or a stuck hold path (INT-03) keeps it closed indefinitely: R_dis is then across a live source - 667 W at 1000 V, 427 W at 800 V - against 100 W continuous / 5 x P for 5 s. Overheating / fire. Contradicts the port design's own requirement on SYS-IO-AUX: K_DISCH 'de-energised only with both contactors open'.
evidence: gen/sys_io_aux.py:675-686 (24V_DO = switch A x switch B; 'K_DISCH (DO5) is held on only while both channels are healthy'); gen/port.py:362-367 (hold from +24V 'which E-stop does not cut'), :413-417 (K_DISCH de-energised = discharging); sim/out/port_design/report.md:95 (667 W peak), :158 (hold up to 197 s, E-stop during a fault), :311 (requirement); Vishay RH overload 5 x P for 5 s (gen/port.py:114 comment); calc 1000^2/1500 = 667 W, 800^2/1500 = 427 W
proposed_fix: Port block (gen/port.py, used by PV-PORT and DAB60): inhibit active discharge in hardware while that port's main contactor is closed - give each port's TPSI3050 its own EN, fed by K_DISCH OR the closed-contactor level (FB_x_MAIN is +24 V through the 1.8 k when the mirror contact opens) through two diodes - and add a thermal cut-off on R_dis for a welded precharge relay. SYS-IO-AUX can then keep cutting K_DISCH unconditionally.

signal_or_function: FB_A_MAIN / FB_B_MAIN (DI4 / DI5) return path
finding: Contactor feedback cannot be read as drawn. The port board sources FB from its PELV +24V through 1.8 k (return = port GND); SYS-IO-AUX reads it on an isolated sinking ISO1212 input whose current returns to DIF_GND, a separate field-ground domain. The harness (drawn nowhere; built by DO/DI name) joins the port GND pins only to the DO-terminal GND, so the DI current has no return inside the module: FB reads 0 = 'open' whatever the contactor does (it works only if the cabinet happens to tie the DI field 0 V to the module 24 V return). The port design requires 'DI field return = module 24 V return (GND)'; SYS-IO-AUX keeps DIF_GND isolated. Lost: weld detection (D-019) and the stuck-hold detection the port design relies on; 'always open' is the unsafe default for weld detection.
evidence: gen/check_interfaces.py HARN lines (all three modules); gen/sys_io_aux.py:510-534 ('DIF_GND = field 0 V (separate domain)', ISO1212 FGND1/FGND2 on DIF_GND); gen/port.py:360 (1.8 k from +24V), :517-521 (J_CTRL pins 10-12 = GND); sim/out/port_design/report.md:311; ISO1212 SLLSEY7G pin table (FGND = field-side ground)
proposed_fix: Decide the DI reference in gen/interfaces.py (DI comment): either (a) the harness joins port-board GND to the DI field return (SYS-IO-AUX J_MC10 pins 9/10) and SYS-IO-AUX documents DIF_GND as bonded to the 24 V return, or (b) the port board passes the mirror contact as a dry contact and SYS-IO-AUX wets it from a field 24 V terminal (polarity inverts: update the contract). Put the return conductor in the gen/build_all.py harness lines.

signal_or_function: hold-closed interlock stuck active (single part)
finding: One shorted part in the hold path (DMP4065S D-S, BSS138BK, LVC1G11 output stuck high) energises the HVC43 coil from the port board's +24V, which no E-stop channel, trip, watchdog or firmware removes (CTRL feeds P_24V unswitched). The contactor then closes as soon as the port board is powered - before precharge, onto an empty bus (kA-class inrush, weld risk) - and can never be opened: the E-stop no longer isolates that port and INT-01 puts R_dis across the live port indefinitely. Gates still go off (both channels) and the other port opens, but nothing else breaks this port's circuit except the fuses. Detection is assumed via FB ('CTRL sees FB = closed against an open command'), which does not work (INT-02); only a firmware VA/VAX comparison remains. Also no diversity: the same AMC3302 feeds the CTRL SC trip, so a stuck current sensor with DIAG valid disables both the SC trip and the hold.
evidence: gen/port.py:378-392 (TLV3502 -> LVC1G32 -> LVC1G11 -> BSS138BK -> DMP4065S from +24V -> S2M -> coil, parallel to the DO feed); gen/ctrl_c2000.py:826 (P_24V through a PTC from the unswitched +24V); sim/out/port_design/report.md:158 ('a shorted DMP4065S keeps the contactor closed ... needs the ISO 13849 analysis'); SYS-IO-AUX_safety_fmea.csv covers SYS parts only
proposed_fix: Port block: require two independent switches for coil current - add a low-side coil switch that conducts only for (K_x_MAIN energised) OR (hold active from an independent second logic path) - so one shorted switch cannot energise the coil; firmware checks VA vs VAX and FB before enabling precharge; include the hold path and the port feedback in the safety-chain FMEA.

signal_or_function: CMPSS hardware trips (port OV, port SC, cell / DAB OC windows)
finding: The CMPSS DACs can use only VDDA (TPS7A2033, +/-1.5 %) as reference because the VDAC pin (ADCINB0) carries P_VBX, and the comparators add +/-20 mV input offset; neither is in any trip budget. Port OV 1100 V trips anywhere in 1031-1169 V uncalibrated, and even after a zero-input offset calibration in 1077-1124 V (chain 0.64 % included): bus 1153 V, device 1466 V = 0.862 x V_DSS against the 0.85 rule the PV design closed at 0.845 with an exact 1100 V trip; the low end lies under the 1050 V firmware OV. Cell OC window 72.4 A: 62.0-82.8 A uncalibrated - below the 62.4 A normal inductor peak (nuisance trips at full load). Port SC 405 A: 374-436 A.
evidence: SPRSP14E 7.11.3.1.1 p170 (offset +/-20 mV), Table 6-1 p18 (ADCINB0 = VDAC), 7.11.3 (DAC reference VDDA or VDAC); TPS7A20 SBVS338 5.5 (DBV, >= 2.8 V: +/-1.5 %); gen/ctrl_c2000.py:423 (P_VBX on ADCINB0), :596 (TPS7A2033 = VDDA); hardware/PVCELL-25/outputs/PVCELL-25_design_check.txt (bus 1129 V, device 0.844 x V_DSS); calc: 0.957 mV/V and 4.945 mV/A at the ADC, error = (1.5 % x V_cmp + 20 mV) / slope
proposed_fix: CTRL-C2000: move P_VBX to the unused ADCIN15 (ball U4), tie ADCINB0/VDAC to VREF2V5 with >= 1 uF and select VDAC as CMPSS reference (ratiometric with the ADC); firmware nulls each CMPSS offset at zero input at start-up; re-budget the 1100 V trip with the residual and place the CMPSS OC window above the cell's local 69.0-76.1 A band.

signal_or_function: PORT +24V (P_24V) feeding the hold-closed path
finding: The hold-closed path draws 0.54-0.57 A (two 96 ohm HVC43 coils + sensor supply) for up to 197 s from P_24V, which CTRL feeds through an MF-MSMF110/33X PTC whose hold current is 0.73 A at 60 C, 0.63 A at 70 C and 0.50 A at 85 C. At the 60 C module ambient plus internal rise the margin is gone; a PTC trip drops the coils while 382-450 A flow, so the contactor opens beyond its breaking capability - the failure D-019 exists to prevent. The port design asks CTRL to 'supply up to 0.6 A while both hold paths are active'.

signal_or_function: loss of port measurements (PORT cable, one conductor, P_24V PTC, +3V3S)

In the PV modules the 1100 V port OV (load rejection) and the 405/450 A SC trips exist only as CMPSS on these channels (no local comparator on PV-PORT or PVCELL), while the cells keep switching on their own cables: one connector or conductor fault removes the over-voltage protection. signal_or_function: AUX-HV backup loop after an opto failure vs the 24 V OV cut-off
finding: If the AUX-HV feedback opto fails, the backup loop settles anywhere in 23.8-28.5 V and AUX-HV becomes the highest source on 24V_OR. Above 26.13-26.42 V the single OV detector on the ORed bus opens all eight branch eFuses (CTRL +24V, +24V_GD, 24V_DO, fans); the cabinet feeds' LM74700s are reverse-biased and AUX-HV keeps the bus up, so the module stays off (CTRL unpowered, no communication) although the cabinet 24 V is healthy. In the 23.8-26.1 V part AUX-HV instead carries the whole module in current limit (INT-09/10). The AUX-HV report's statement that the OV cut-off 'disconnects the feed' is not what the SYS circuit does: it disconnects the loads.
evidence: sim/out/aux_hv_design/report.md sec. 7 (backup 26.1 V, band 23.8-28.5 V; PG OV flag 24.93-25.54 V); gen/sys_io_aux.py:299-310 (one LM2903B OV comparator on 24V_OR -> OV_CUT), :328-334 (OVP = OV_CUT on every TPS16630), :262-279 (feed 3 = LM74700 + one CSD18532: no disconnect, the body diode conducts forward)
proposed_fix: SYS-IO-AUX feed 3: an ideal-diode controller with load disconnect and OV cut-off (e.g. LM74800-Q1 / LM74810-Q1, back-to-back FETs) set below 26.0 V, so a faulty AUX-HV is isolated and the cabinet feeds keep the module running; AUX-HV may add a latching secondary OV shutdown below 26.0 V.

signal_or_function: power budget from AUX-HV alone; fan default at start-up
finding: AUX-HV (30 W rated; peak-current limit 34 W worst / 58 W typ) cannot run any module: at power PV-P75 needs ~64 W (100 W bound), PV-P100 ~77 W, DAB-D60 ~43 W (logic 13 W + gate-drive bias 8-14 W per cell / 11-19 W per bridge + 10 W for two HVC43 coils + fans 17-23 W). From AUX-HV alone only standby (13 W) plus either the two closed contactors (23 W) or the idle bias of three cells (25 W) fits, not both (35 W). First start from HV fails for the PV modules: SYS-IO-AUX fans default ON (FAN_EN 10 k pull-up, PWM open = full speed), so 3-4 x 12 W plus CTRL switch on at the 16.1 V eFuse UVLO = 48-60 W > 34 W; the bus is pulled back under the 15.0 V UVLO and cycles (the AUX-HV start-up analysis assumes 30 W there, A-17; DAB-D60 with no fans, ~11 W, starts). The SYS hand-over note ('firmware must then shed fans') and the AUX-HV report ('SYS eFuses (CTRL branch 4.5 A) bound the real load' - the CTRL branch is 1.98 A and AUX-HV feeds the whole bus) overstate what fits.

REQUIREMENTS / interfaces.AUX: state what must run from AUX-HV alone (proposed: standby, communications and the closed contactors, no power conversion) or resize AUX-HV to >= 80 W (PV-P75) / 100 W (PV-P100).

signal_or_function: watchdog first kick after XRSn release
finding: The TPS3850 needs the first WDI edge within tWDU(min) = 165.8 ms of every release of RESET or WDO, and SYS_RST_N is CTRL's XRSn: if boot-to-first-kick ever exceeds 165.8 ms, each WDO pulse resets CTRL again and the module never starts. The SYS-IO-AUX firmware start-up list does not state this limit. (Slow AUX-HV ramp: no extra risk - CTRL is powered only above the 16.1 V eFuse UVLO and SYS_RST_N is held low by the dead CTRL until then.)

proposed_fix: Add to the firmware requirements: first WDI edge <= 150 ms after XRSn release, then every 10.35-165.8 ms.

signal_or_function: FLT while EN is low (fault latch PRE + CLR both active)

The PVCELL note says 'a fault still present re-sets it'.

proposed_fix: AND the live trip condition into FLT (FLT_OK = ... AND PRE_N / TRIP_N) so a standing fault is visible with EN low; correct the PVCELL block note.
